story: The Air Force is offering about 4,700 acres of Alaska federal land for commercial AI data center development, and no power, water or project-size figure for those parcels has been published anywhere a resident can read.
fact_check: two adversarial validators, 2026-09-23. Federal track verified in full. Anything not in this file may not appear on screen or in the VO.

claims.spoken: The Air Force is offering about four thousand seven hundred acres of federal land in Alaska.
claims.verbatim_source: "It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet."
claims.source_label: Alaska Public Media / American Homefront Project, September 15th
requires: the word ABOUT or ROUGHLY stays attached to the number, on screen and in VO. It is an offer figure, not a survey.

claims.verbatim_source: "Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development"
claims.source_label: Air and Space Forces Magazine, April 11th
claims.label: per Air and Space Forces Magazine
requires: NEVER say twelve data centers. A separate outlet says 'up to a dozen data centers' and that is a different claim about a different thing.
the map may show the THREE INSTALLATIONS and may NOT show twelve located dots. Their locations are not public (see c4).

claims.spoken: The solicitation is A F C E C dash twenty six dash R dash zero zero zero six. Proposals closed June twenty ninth.
claims.verbatim_source: field: "AFCEC-26-R-0006, Air Force Installation Contracting Agency, posted April 10, 2026, response due June 29, 2026, extended from May 29, 2026"
claims.source_label: HigherGov mirror of the SAM.gov notice
claims.label: solicitation record
requires: this is a REQUEST FOR LEASE PROPOSAL. Never say the Air Force is BUILDING anything. It is offering LAND.
SAM.gov itself would not render, so this is a near-primary mirror and is labeled as a record rather than quoted as the government's own page.

claims.note: Any per-base parcel breakdown. Five at Eielson, two across the Richardson Highway, one near southeast North Pole. NOTHING readable supports it. It may not appear as a number, a map label, or a count of pins in the animation.

claims.spoken: Salcha resident Sarah Hollister told reporters the roar of jet fighters always reminded her of the sacrifices we make for freedom. But the hum of a data center, she said, shows her we have completely lost our way.
claims.on_screen: But the sound of a 24/7 hum from a data center shows me that we have completely lost our way.
claims.verbatim_source: "The roar of jet fighters and helicopters overhead has always reminded me of our sacrifices we make for freedom," she said. "But the sound of a 24/7 hum from a data center shows me that we have completely lost our way."
claims.source_label: Sarah Hollister, Salcha resident, to Alaska Public Media / American Homefront Project
claims.label: Sarah Hollister, Salcha resident
requires: SHE SAID THIS TO A REPORTER ON A NEIGHBOURHOOD TRAIL, NOT AS ASSEMBLY TESTIMONY. Labelling it testimony would be a fabricated setting and it nearly shipped.
it is TWO sentences on the page. On screen use the second sentence ALONE so nothing is stitched.
this is HER sentiment and the film lets her own it. It is not the house position, and Interior Alaska's relationship with Eielson is genuinely two-sided (see c12).

claims.spoken: Senator Lisa Murkowski said she is not a proponent of data centers at J B E R or at the Interior installations, because Alaska can't support them on an insecure energy base.
claims.on_screen: I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations
claims.verbatim_source: "I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time."
claims.source_label: Sen. Lisa Murkowski, as quoted by Alaska Public Media
claims.label: Sen. Lisa Murkowski, as quoted by Alaska Public Media
requires: the fragment beginning 'because we are not able to support them' may NOT stand alone. Without its subject it reads as someone else's 'we'.
capital I on Interior. It is a region.
her position is CONDITIONAL, tied to the energy base. Do not render her as an opponent of data centers generally.
no date or venue for the remark exists in any source. The film may not say when or where she said it.

claims.spoken: In late August the Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly asked for a pause on large commercial data centers. K U A C reports it was the only item that appears on both the state and the federal list.
claims.on_screen: THE ONLY ITEM ON BOTH LISTS
claims.verbatim_source: "But only one item appears as a priority in both state and federal parts of the list – a request to temporarily halt the development of large commercial data centers in Alaska."
claims.label: per KUAC
requires: say LATE AUGUST. KUAC prints only 'Thursday'. August 27th is arithmetic, not a printed fact, and may not go on screen as a date.
it is a REQUEST on a legislative wish list aimed at Congress and the Legislature. The borough did NOT impose or pass a moratorium. Never say it did.
the ask covers large commercial data centers in Alaska generally, which is broader than military land.

claims.spoken: At least a hundred communities around the country have already adopted data center moratoriums.
claims.verbatim_source: "At least 100 communities across the nation have adopted moratoria on building them, as opposition spreads from local jurisdictions to state legislatures."
claims.source_label: American Homefront Project, citing a Columbia Law School analysis
claims.label: per a Columbia Law School analysis, via the American Homefront Project
requires: keep AT LEAST. Never round to 'more than 100'.
do NOT animate a counter. It is a May figure quoted in September, so it is a stale floor, and the underlying post body was unreachable.

claims.spoken: The Assembly can ask. As the reporting puts it, it can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land.
claims.on_screen: it can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation, the reporters' own characterization: "Even though the Borough Assembly is calling for a data center moratorium, it can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land."
claims.label: as the reporting puts it
requires: THIS IS THE WEAKEST LOAD-BEARING ELEMENT AND IT IS REPORTING, NOT LAW. No lawyer, statute, case or borough attorney is quoted anywhere readable.
use MAY BE POWERLESS, matching the outlet's own headline. NEVER 'has no power'.
the borough's actual ask is a state and federal moratorium, a lobbying route that does not depend on borough zoning power at all, so 'powerless' overstates the borough's own framing.

claims.spoken: As of the middle of September, no projects had been awarded.
claims.verbatim_source: "though no projects have been awarded yet"
claims.label: as of September 15th
requires: TIME-BOUND IT. Never the bare present tense. SAM.gov could not be checked for a later award notice.

claims.spoken: No megawatt figure. No water figure. No project size. For these parcels, none of it has been published.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation, an absence confirmed across every readable source. Air and Space Forces Magazine speaks only generically: "consume large amounts of electricity and water".
claims.source_label: absence confirmed across five readable sources by the validator
claims.label: not disclosed
requires: THE FILM MAY NOT ESTIMATE, MODEL, BENCHMARK AGAINST ANOTHER DATA CENTER, OR ANIMATE A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER. Any on-screen capacity or water slot reads NOT DISCLOSED.
the honest ceiling is 'not published anywhere a resident can open'. The DAF release and the News-Miner were unreachable, so the absence is not claimed as absolute.

claims.spoken: Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins says his community was buoyed by defense spending and infrastructure when the F thirty five squadron arrived.
claims.on_screen: Our community was buoyed by defense spending and infrastructure as the F-35 fighter squadron was placed here.
claims.verbatim_source: "Our community was buoyed by defense spending and infrastructure as the F-35 fighter squadron was placed here."
claims.source_label: Grier Hopkins, Fairbanks North Star Borough mayor
requires: HOPKINS IS NOT QUOTED OPPOSING THE DATA CENTERS. Cutting him beside Hollister as a second voice of opposition would misrepresent him.
he is the evidence that this military community's relationship with its bases is two-sided.

claims.spoken: The Air Force calls it a public private partnership that supports the readiness of its Airmen and Guardians.
claims.on_screen: generating value that directly supports our missions
claims.verbatim_source: "This is a unique opportunity for a true public-private partnership. By making this land available, we are supporting the growing demands of the AI industry while generating value that directly supports our missions and the readiness of our Airmen and Guardians."
claims.source_label: Robert Moriarty, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations, April 11th
requires: this is the strongest fair point FOR the offer and Act 3 owes it a real scene, not a clause.

claims.spoken: The developer carries the financing, the permitting, the construction and the long term operation.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation, the magazine's summary of the solicitation: the selected developer "will be responsible for all aspects of the project, including financing, permitting, construction and long-term operation"
claims.source_label: Air and Space Forces Magazine, April 11th
requires: part of the Act 3 case FOR. The risk sits with the developer, not the taxpayer.

claims.spoken: Fairbanks already has some of the highest utility costs in the country.
claims.on_screen: SOME OF THE NATION'S HIGHEST UTILITY COSTS
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska's energy system is strained, and Fairbanks already has some of the nation's highest utility costs."
requires: no dollar figure is published in the source. Do not supply one.

cultural_rules: NO ALASKA NATIVE VOICE APPEARS IN ANY SOURCE. The film must not imply Native support, Native opposition, or a unified Interior position. Silence in the sourcing is silence, not consent.

Eielson sits above Salcha and Clear sits near Nenana and Anderson, in the traditional territory of Lower Tanana Dene peoples, and the water at issue is the Tanana River system. If the film uses water imagery it is depicting a subsistence and fishery watershed, not scenery, and it may put no number on that draw.
Never the word invasion, and no framing of outside tech arriving on Native land. No source supports it and it would put words in absent mouths.
Do not render the military-town audience as uniformly angry. Hopkins' F-35 line is the counter-evidence in the same reporting.
banned_from_screen: any per-base parcel breakdown or twelve located map dots
any megawatt, water, acre-foot, gallons-per-day or project-size figure
the date or venue of Murkowski's remark
Hollister's trail quote labelled as Assembly testimony
any flat assertion that the borough has no legal authority
an animated counter on the 100 communities figure
anything attributed to the Department of the Air Force's own release, which was never readable
